---
name: my-skill
description: Use this skill whenever you build or change any page of Third Place, a Lahore city atlas that helps people find places to spend time that aren't home, university or work.
---

1. The brand is written "THIRD PLACE" in small, widely spaced serif capitals, with the subtitle "The Lahore Atlas". The home page headline is "A guide to the spaces between".
2. Tone of voice is literary, calm and precise, like the notes in an old survey map. Speak to the visitor as "you" and ask about intentions ("somewhere to read", "somewhere to breathe"), never about "categories" or "listings".
3. Colours, taken from old Lahore survey maps and miniature painting: parchment #F0E8D8 (canvas, about 65%), walnut ink #463B35 (text), indigo ink #424E68 (navigation and map lines), Persian sage #879783 (gardens), faded pomegranate #A86F70 (accents), dusty terracotta #B98269 (social spaces), old rose #C7A0A0 (saved items), antique brass #B49A69 (fine details only), walled-city brick #9E4A42, Ravi blue #A7C4CC and garden chartreuse #C9C77F (map washes only). No pure white, no neon, no gradients.
4. Fonts are always thin: headings in "Cormorant Garamond" weight 300, interface text in "Manrope" weight 200–400, and real Urdu words only in "Noto Nastaliq Urdu". Never use bold or heavy weights.
5. Every page must include: the THIRD PLACE wordmark with its arch emblem, atlas-style navigation (Discover, The Atlas, Collections, My Places, Colophon), a faint survey-linework background, and a footer with a scale bar and "Surveyed in Lahore" plus the year.
6. Sections are entered through the gates of the Walled City: label each one with a gate name and a Roman numeral (for example "Roshnai Gate · I"). Lists and steps use circled numerals (①, ②, ③).
7. Prices are written as "Rs. 500" or "Rs. 500–1,000" (comma for thousands, en dash for ranges); a place with no cost is "Free". Coordinates are written like 31°33′N 74°19′E and distances like "1.2 km".
8. Every place card shows: name, neighbourhood, an original SVG emblem, spend band, noise level, solo-friendliness, a "Before you go" section, a wax-seal save button and a link to directions.
9. Motion is precise and tactile: short, stiff springs, ink that draws itself on scroll, seals that press and recoil. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
10. Forms check phone numbers are 11 digits starting with 03 before they submit.
11. Never invent opening hours, entry fees, phone numbers, reviews or coordinates for a real place. Unknown facts say "Check before you go", and sample notes are labelled as editors' notes.
